title: E-Syn: E-Graph Rewriting with Technology-Aware Cost Functions for Logic Synthesis
problem: Existing multi-level logic optimization algorithms employ greedy approaches with local optimization steps that limit exploration space and miss opportunities for significant improvements. Each step breaks circuits into small pieces (k-feasible cuts) and applies incremental changes separately.
motivation: Logic synthesis plays a crucial role in the digital design flow and has decisive influence on the final Quality of Results (QoR) of circuit implementations.
method: E-Syn uses an e-graph—a data structure that stores multiple equivalent ways to represent the same circuit—to explore many different but logically equivalent designs. It evaluates each design using cost functions tailored to the specific hardware technology being targeted, optimizing for either faster execution speed (lower delay) or smaller chip area. By maintaining all these equivalent options throughout optimization rather than greedily committing to each local choice, E-Syn discovers significantly better overall designs.
key_novelty: Combining e-graphs—data structures that store equivalent circuit representations—with technology-specific cost functions enables exploration of a much wider set of circuit designs than traditional greedy optimization approaches.
contributions: E-Syn framework leveraging e-graphs for efficient logic rewriting in synthesis
Technology-aware cost functions supporting both delay and area optimization
Demonstration of wider design space exploration compared to AIG-based synthesis
15.29% delay savings and 6.42% area savings on benchmark designs
